slides.headline: October 20, 1962: a border conflict began that would reshape how India builds its defenses for the next six decades.
Large-scale fighting broke out along India's northern frontier, in Ladakh and the northeast
slides.body: The conflict exposed gaps in India's border infrastructure, high-altitude logistics and military preparedness - lessons that shaped defense policy for generations afterward.

slides.headline: India rebuilt its approach to border roads, high-altitude supply chains and domestic defense production from the ground up.
slides.body: The Border Roads Organisation's mandate expanded, defense R&D investment grew, and the push toward domestic weapons manufacturing that India still pursues today traces directly back to the gaps this conflict exposed.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs the infrastructure and industrial base to defend itself without depending on others.
slides.body: The decades of investment in border roads, high-altitude logistics and domestic defense manufacturing that followed 1962 are the direct ancestors of the self-reliant defense sector India is still building today.

sources.text: Naval War College Review - The Sino-Indian Border War
